existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: `CompartmentDefinition` has local R4→R6 breaking changes, chiefly removal of `resource.documentation` and required binding changes for `resource.code`. The top migration concerns are resource-type code churn, R6-only `$everything` start/end parameter metadata, and runtime interpretation of `resource.param`. Confidence is high for the computable diffs, with uncertainty around ballot intent and the observed R6 `Group` compartment inconsistency.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Migrations should combine structural transforms and terminology/version-aware validation. R4→R6 transforms need to drop or preserve `resource.documentation` out of band and review all `resource.code` values against the R6 resource-type ValueSet. R6→R4 transforms need extension or sidecar strategies for `title`, `versionAlgorithm[x]`, `resource.startParam`, and `resource.endParam`, and must decide how to handle R6-only compartment and resource codes.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for element presence, cardinality, type, local constraint, and local binding comparisons because both primary StructureDefinitions and relevant local terminology artifacts were present. Confidence is lower for rationale and operational impact because no official diff/JIRA notes or full narrative-page comparison were supplied, and the R6 ballot package appears internally inconsistent about a `Group` compartment code.

rationaleMd:
CompartmentDefinition keeps its resource identity. The aggregate has 2 hard R4-to-R6 instance break(s), 0 potential hard break(s), 1 non-mechanical migration finding(s), and 0 direct behavior/API finding(s).

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 1, which creates weak stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 20/100, producing migration shape `mostly-stable-with-local-breaks`, major migration `No`, and compatibility posture `preserve-compatibility-per-change`.

3 finding(s) identify a yes/partial less-breaking base-design alternative, so the aggregate should not be used to dismiss local avoidability review.

recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Treat this as a mostly stable resource. Individual hard breaks, renames, required bindings, or behavior changes should stand or fall on their own rationale and available less-breaking alternatives.

topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances using removed resource-type codes fail the R6 required binding; runtime/API/codegen updates are also likely for enum switches and compartment-routing tables.

topFindings.title: CompartmentDefinition.resource.documentation was removed
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: strict R6 validators and generated R6 models have no place for `resource.documentation`, so populated R4 rows need deletion, extension mapping, or out-of-band preservation.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: resource.param now explicitly means the core HL7 SearchParameter code, not a server alias
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: JSON shape does not change, but server algorithms or generated rule tables that used local SearchParameter aliases must align to core HL7 codes to preserve compartment behavior.
